Since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=1,$ we will use a step size of 

$$
Δx=1-\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

First, we add the initial condition data:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\frac{1}{2}$ | $1$ |  |  |

Next, we compute ${y}^{′}$ according to the given rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =x(2y-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\cdot 1-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we add this to our table:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\frac{1}{2}$ | $1$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ |  |

Next, we compute $Δy$ using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

We add this to our table:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\frac{1}{2}$ | $1$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ |

To get the values of $x$ and $y$ in the *next* row, we add $Δx$ to $x$ and $Δy$ to $y,$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =1 \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\  & =1+\frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{5}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Adding these rows to our table gives the following:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\frac{1}{2}$ | $1$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ |
| $1$ | $\frac{5}{4}$ |  |  |

Therefore, we conclude that $y(1)≈\frac{5}{4}.$

x y y′ Δy
12 1

Next, we compute y′ according to the given rule: y′=x(2y−1)=12(2⋅1−1)=12

So, we add this to our table:

x y y′ Δy
12 1 12

Next, we compute Δy using Euler's method: Δy=y′⋅Δx=12(12)=14

We add this to our table:

x y y′ Δy
12 1 12 14

To get the values of x and y in the next row, we add Δx to x and Δy to y, as follows: xnew=x+Δx=12+12=1ynew=y+Δy=1+14=54

Adding these rows to our table gives the following:

x y y′ Δy
12 1 12 14
1 54

Therefore, we conclude that y(1)≈54.
